content:
- Model consistently underestimates true prices in the early part of the 30-day horizon, especially after recent spikes.
- Model overestimates prices in the middle to late horizon when true prices show sharp downward or sideways corrections.
- Model exhibits lag in reacting to sudden price spikes; forecasts remain high for several days after a spike.
- Model fails to capture mean reversion in the final 5–10 days of the horizon, often staying too high when prices should decline.
- Model tends to overcorrect after minor corrections, leading to overshoots in the 2nd–3rd day of the horizon.
- Model underestimates the magnitude of true price increases during periods of high volatility or policy-driven spikes.
- Model shows persistent bias toward lower values in the first 5–7 days of the horizon, especially when recent history is volatile.
